title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, document pipeline semantics, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI to accelerate NetOps. However, automated configuration generation creates operational risk when outputs violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs can magnify these risks. Prior prototype studies show that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and targeted repair can reduce observable errors, but many evaluations report token- or reference-match metrics that do not directly measure deployability or deterministic-validator acceptance. This paper asks a narrowly scoped, operational question amenable to preregistered inference: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The study cand-2026-03 preregistered a single formal estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and a confirmatory paired exact McNemar test. Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end; (2) an explicit, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics under shared_initial_candidate generation; (3) quantitative confirmatory results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in deterministic-validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; and (4) explicit reconciliation of preregistration wording with the formal estimand and disclosure of a protocol deviation (unset temperature).
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow, NetPlumber-style approaches) offer semantics-focused acceptance criteria that check forwarding, access-control, and ordering invariants and therefore are natural deployment gates for generated configurations [1,2,3]. Prior LLM-for-NetOps evaluations (NetConfEval, NetLLMBench, and related studies) document that model-only generation produces syntactic and higher-level semantic mistakes (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches), and they emphasize the limitations of token-level metrics for measuring deployability [4,5,6]. Generate–validate–repair architectures, and Toolformer-style orchestration, have been proposed and demonstrated in prototype settings: an LLM produces a candidate, a verifier checks it, and constrained repair prompts are issued when diagnostics are actionable [7,3]. Security work on prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks highlights the need for input-sanitization and gating defenses in pipelines that accept external or operator-supplied text [8]. Surveys of AIOps and LLM applicability to telecommunications call for more operationally grounded benchmarks that measure deployability and validator acceptance rather than surface similarity alone [4]. These prior findings motivated a preregistered experiment that uses deterministic-validator acceptance as the primary estimand and explicitly records per-episode validator traces for diagnostic analysis.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent define a binary outcome equal to 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes across Baseline and Guarded). Synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN updates, and required sequencing constraints (shutdown–change–restore patterns). The adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates; generation seeds and mutation taxonomy are archived. Scope is limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in our validator; no production operator data were used.

Model, validator, and orchestration. Declared generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter implementing a generate–validate–repair workflow. The guarded branch applied a template-based input sanitizer prior to gating; the guarded policy permitted at most one automated repair call per pair. The archived model configuration recorded temperature = null; this unset sampling parameter is disclosed as a protocol deviation (see Disclosure). To preserve paired comparability the preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (single shared LLM draft per pair) so downstream effects (sanitization, gating, possible repair, final validation) are the causal factors under test.

Missingness and exclusions. The missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). Provider-call accounting and per-episode failure logs were archived and used to apply the preregistered exclusion rule. Important preregistered but unexecuted items: the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are computed or reported here. This omission is explicitly noted because it constrains interpretation of potential blocking of benign intents by the guarded pipeline (see Results and Limitations).
sections.results:
Execution and counts. The archived execution completed 282 of the planned 300 episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons and were recorded per the preregistered missingness_plan. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures) 141 complete pairs entered the primary confirmatory analysis (complete_pairs = 141; both_missing_pairs = 9). Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 156 (completed = 147; failed = 9); stage_counts show shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 6.

Primary outcomes and inference. Condition summary: baseline_successes = 135/141 (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383); guarded_successes = 141/141 (guarded success rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (complete pairs): n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar) yields p = 0.03125. The paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numbers and test parameters are archived and reproducible from the analysis artifacts.

Diagnostics for discordant cases. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable: for each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate is identical between baseline and guarded artifacts, and repair-stage activity links to the guarded acceptance in these pairs (repair stage_count = 6). For discordant pairs the guarded pipeline converted an initial draft the validator would reject into a final candidate the validator accepted via sanitizer normalization and/or the single permitted automated repair. The scoring artifacts explicitly record repair_applied when a repair call produced the accepted final candidate. These diagnostics show that the guarded pipeline's higher acceptance arose from permitted recovery actions rather than baseline rejections becoming permanent under guarded gating.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. As a conservative sensitivity check, treating those excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this conservative accounting reduces effective rates but does not invert the direction of the observed paired difference. Note again: the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) was not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking statistics are available in this run and claims about the guarded pipeline's effect on benign intents cannot be supported by the present data.
sections.discussion:
Interpretive reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 framed verifier-gating as reducing attacker success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These differ conceptually: higher validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline can reflect successful repair of reparable, benign drafts and does not by itself demonstrate reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. Our diagnostics show the six discordant conversions involved permitted repair or sanitizer normalization that produced validator-accepted candidates; practitioners should therefore treat validator acceptance as a partial proxy for deployability but not as a standalone measure of attacker defeat without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Practical significance given ceiling effects. The observed absolute paired increase ≈ 4.26 percentage points occurred against a high baseline acceptance (≈95.7%), producing a ceiling effect: a small absolute improvement is statistically detectable but may have limited operational impact in contexts where baseline acceptance is already high. The discordant-count (n10 = 6) is small in absolute terms, so operators should evaluate whether bounded repair-induced acceptance gains justify potential risks of repair masking adversarial manipulations.

Operational recommendations. (1) Treat sanitizer, gating, and repair as a co-design problem: define validator coverage, permitted-repair scope, and gating invariants jointly to avoid repairs that mask adversarial intent. (2) Execute the preregistered benign-control in future runs to measure false-positive blocking empirically. (3) Diversify generators and validators (vendor CLI dialects, BGP/MPLS semantics) before extrapolating to production. (4) For deterministic reproduction set explicit sampling to temperature = 0 (the archived run recorded temperature = null).
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls or sanitizer normalization that enabled acceptance. Importantly, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, technical failures that reduced effective sample size, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair). The archived execution and analysis manifests contain the machine-verifiable artifacts and per-episode traces; those artifacts support the numeric claims made in this paper. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
